what_its_for: Ceftazidime-avibactam is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain urinary tract infections (including kidney infections), abdominal infections (such as infections in your belly or intestines), and hospital-acquired or ventilator-associated pneumonia (lung infections). It works by killing bacteria that are resistant to many other antibiotics. It does NOT treat viral infections like the cold or flu.
how_to_take: This medicine is given directly into your vein (intravenously, or IV) by a nurse or healthcare provider, usually in a hospital or infusion center. Each dose is given slowly over 2 hours as an IV infusion. You will not take this medicine by mouth. Your healthcare team will prepare and administer each dose for you. Make sure to tell your nurse if the IV site becomes red, swollen, or painful during the infusion.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 2.5 grams (ceftazidime 2 g plus avibactam 0.5 g) given every 8 hours (three times a day) by IV infusion over 2 hours. Your dose may be adjusted if you have kidney problems. The length of treatment is usually 5 to 14 days depending on the type of infection you have. Always follow the exact dosing schedule your doctor or healthcare team has prescribed for you.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given to you by a healthcare provider in a clinical setting, it is unlikely that you will miss a dose. However, if a dose is missed or delayed, contact your nurse, doctor, or infusion center right away so they can reschedule it as soon as possible. Do not try to double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: You do not need to store this medication yourself, as it is prepared and stored by the hospital or infusion center pharmacy. If you are receiving infusions at home, your home infusion pharmacy will provide specific storage instructions. In general, the prepared IV solution should be refrigerated and used within the time frame your pharmacist specifies. Keep all medications out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about ALL medications you take, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements, before starting this antibiotic. Avoid taking chloramphenicol (another antibiotic) at the same time, as it may interfere with how this medicine works. Do not stop your antibiotic treatment early even if you feel better, as this can allow the infection to return or become harder to treat. Avoid drinking alcohol during your treatment as it may worsen side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness); severe diarrhea or diarrhea that is watery or bloody, which could be a sign of a serious bowel infection called C. difficile; seizures or unusual shaking; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination, swelling in your legs or feet; confusion, hallucinations, or unusual changes in behavior; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); or any new or worsening symptoms during treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting treatment, but it is very important to complete your full course of antibiotics even if you feel well. Most patients see significant improvement within 3 to 7 days. Your doctor will monitor your progress with lab tests and physical exams. If your symptoms are not improving or are getting worse after 2 to 3 days, let your healthcare team know right away.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your dose will likely be reduced if your kidneys are not working well, so your doctor will check your kidney function during treatment. Elderly patients: Older adults may need a lower dose because kidney function naturally decreases with age. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Use only if clearly needed and your doctor determines the benefits outweigh the risks. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine can be used in infants and children 3 months of age and older at doses adjusted for their weight and kidney function.
